subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should #99449 close into the session-state resolver and stale OpenAI route trackers now, or remain open as the concrete Codex-plugin hot-reload reproduction until live proof pins the trigger?
rationale: Source inspection proves OpenAI-selected sessions become Codex when the harness is registered, but it does not prove whether this report is only an explicit/stale OpenAI pin or a distinct Codex enablement bug for DeepSeek-primary sessions.

options.title: Keep as concrete repro
options.body: Leave #99449 open and ask the investigator to attach a live repro or PR proving the DeepSeek-primary hot-reload trigger before deciding duplicate closure.

options.title: Fold into #87957
options.body: Close this as duplicate of the broad session-state resolver if maintainers accept that the remaining work is fully covered by selected/runtime/auth state centralization.

options.title: Retarget to #101672
options.body: Close this into the narrower stale literal OpenAI route repair if live evidence confirms an automatic `providerOverride: "openai"` pin is the whole cause.

recommendation.title: Keep as concrete repro
recommendation.body: Leave #99449 open and ask the investigator to attach a live repro or PR proving the DeepSeek-primary hot-reload trigger before deciding duplicate closure.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the recent OpenAI provider identity and Codex runtime boundary where steipete has the strongest current history signal.
